scenes.tts: Here is a loop. When N F kappa B switches on, one of its target genes encodes tumor necrosis factor, or T N F. T N F is a cytokine, which is a signaling protein that immune cells secrete. Where does it go next?
scenes.caption: Here is a loop. When NF-κB switches on, one of its target genes encodes tumor necrosis factor, or TNF. TNF is a cytokine, which is a signaling protein that immune cells secrete. Where does it go next?
scenes.visual: A cell with a nucleus: NF-kB sits on DNA beside three genes; one gene is named TNF and releases orange TNF capsules that leave the cell through the membrane.
scenes.narration: Here is a loop. When NF-κB switches on, one of its target genes encodes tumor necrosis factor, or TNF. TNF is a cytokine, which is a signaling protein that immune cells secrete. Where does it go next?

scenes.tts: T N F binds T N F receptor 1 on the same cell, and on its neighbors. That receptor also signals to I K K and N F kappa B. So the alarm spreads. But this receptor carries a second message.
scenes.caption: TNF binds TNF receptor 1 on the same cell, and on its neighbors. That receptor also signals to IKK and NF-κB. So the alarm spreads. But this receptor carries a second message.
scenes.visual: Three cells in a row; TNF capsules land on the receptor of the middle cell, then of both neighbors; in each, an arrow runs receptor to IKK to NF-kB and NF-kB lights up.
scenes.narration: TNF binds TNF receptor 1 on the same cell, and on its neighbors. That receptor also signals to IKK and NF-κB. So the alarm spreads. But this receptor carries a second message.

scenes.tts: T N F receptor 1 is a death receptor. It can instruct a cell to kill itself. Usually it does not. N F kappa B switches on genes whose products block the death machinery. So the receptor says die and stay alive at once. The second message normally wins.
scenes.caption: TNF receptor 1 is a death receptor. It can instruct a cell to kill itself. Usually it does not. NF-κB switches on genes whose products block the death machinery. So the receptor says die and stay alive at once. The second message normally wins.
scenes.visual: One large receptor with TNF bound: a magenta die arm runs to death machinery; a green stay-alive arm runs through NF-kB to genes that block the death machinery with a T-bar; the die arm dims and the cell usually survives.
scenes.narration: TNF receptor 1 is a death receptor. It can instruct a cell to kill itself. Usually it does not. NF-κB switches on genes whose products block the death machinery. So the receptor says die and stay alive at once. The second message normally wins.

scenes.tts: Now take cultured cells whose N F kappa B arm is blocked, for example by an I kappa B that cannot be phosphorylated. The same T N F kills. The death arm belongs to a later lesson. Keep this rule. N F kappa B normally makes the stay-alive message win.
scenes.caption: Now take cultured cells whose NF-κB arm is blocked, for example by an IκB that cannot be phosphorylated. The same TNF kills. The death arm belongs to a later lesson. Keep this rule. NF-κB normally makes the stay-alive message win.
scenes.visual: The same diagram in cultured cells: a red IκB with a crossed-out phosphate sits on NF-kB, the survival arm is cut, the T-bar is gone and the die arm reaches the cell, which is killed; a note says the death arm is a later lesson; the rule appears.
scenes.narration: Now take cultured cells whose NF-κB arm is blocked, for example by an IκB that cannot be phosphorylated. The same TNF kills. The death arm belongs to a later lesson. Keep this rule. NF-κB normally makes the stay-alive message win.
